text: Chivor is a town and municipality in the Eastern Boyacá Province, within the Colombian department of Boyacá. It is situated at 215 kilometres (134 mi) from the department capital, Tunja, and has a mean temperature of 18 °C (64 °F) in the Tenza Valley. The municipality is bordered to the north by Macanal, to the south by Ubalá, Cundinamarca, to the east by Santa María, and to the west by Almeida. The name Chivor originates from the Chibcha language and means "Our farmfields - our mother" or "Green and rich land," the latter referring to the abundant emerald deposits. The area was inhabited by the Muisca prior to the Spanish conquest, who were part of the Muisca Confederation, with the zaque of Hunza in the north and the zipa of Bacatá in the south. The Muisca already knew and mined the rich emerald deposits, using emeralds as religious offerings, decorations, and currency. Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada discovered the emerald deposits in 1537, but the mines were abandoned until 1886. Modern Chivor was officially founded on December 16, 1930, by Florencio Novoa. Its main economic activities are agriculture, including maize, yuca, bananas, sugarcane, beans, chayote, coffee, and fruits such as papayas, blackberries, lulo, and tree tomatoes, as well as emerald mining. In 2014, emeralds worth 30 million US dollars were extracted in Boyacá, and the rich deposits have led to numerous regional conflicts, including in Chivor. The Gran Esmeralda de Moctezuma, a 21-centimetre (8.3 in) high, 17-centimetre (6.7 in) long, and 16-centimetre (6.3 in) thick emerald, was found in Chivor and is currently in Vienna, Austria. Other notable emeralds from Chivor include Patricia, weighing 632 carats (126.4 grams or 4.46 oz), and La Magnífica, measuring 1225 carats (245 grams or 8.6 oz). The Embalse la Esmeralda, a hydroelectric reservoir governed from Chivor, Macanal, and Almeida, produces hydroelectric energy. Chivor has a subtropical highland climate (Cfb) characterized by heavy to very heavy rainfall throughout the year.
